profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility is located at 1755 Old Meadow Road, McLean, VA 22102, one of two adjacent Lumen buildings on Old Meadow Road (the other at 1757, also tracked in this registry), part of the broader Tysons/McLean data center and telecommunications corridor near Washington, DC; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Northern Virginia facility. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that will raise a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers effective January 1, 2027; regulators approved $775.6 million of the roughly $1.2 billion Dominion sought, cutting about $350 million tied to speculative data center projects, according to Inside Climate News.

The Tysons/McLean corridor has long served as a network interconnection hub for the Washington, DC metro, predating much of the newer hyperscale build-out further west in Loudoun County; Lumen's two adjacent Old Meadow Road buildings reflect that older, carrier-hotel-style pattern of data center development.

reading.body:
Lumen McLean is a carrier-hotel colocation facility at 1755 Old Meadow Road in McLean, Virginia, one of two adjacent Lumen buildings in the Tysons/McLean network corridor near Washington, DC. Lumen does not publish capacity, square footage, or power specifications for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites, including this one. The facility offers cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described by Lumen as varying by site, a specification too broad to estimate total campus draw or rack density without additional data.

The Tysons/McLean corridor reflects an older pattern of carrier-hotel development predating the hyperscale expansion further west in Loudoun County. Virginia's published data center capacity totals 1,375 megawatts across 23 facilities with disclosed specs; Lumen McLean, like 307 other mapped sites in the state, publishes no figure and therefore cannot be ranked against the state's hyperscale capacity. The facility operates within a grid now shaped by Virginia's January 2027 data center rate class, approved by regulators in November 2026 as a formal acknowledgment that data center electricity demand is reshaping statewide rates.

Without published capacity, Lumen McLean cannot be assessed for relevance to AI scaling. The site matters to network operations and edge services in the DC metro, the historical purpose of the Tysons corridor, but its contribution to the compute constraints binding AI infrastructure remains unknown and therefore absent from any ranking of capacity concentration.
